ratings.reason: The merge of an original input's style with target latent codes is suggestive of fusion and was relatively distinctive in 2022. However, the quote describes synthesis internals rather than a user separately selecting operands and invoking a same-space operator, so its fit and impact are only partially supported.

Reference recombination is central according to the title, and extracting aspects from multiple references could transfer broadly. But the quoted introduction only defines recombination; it does not show CreativeConnect's operand-selection interaction, operator, or resulting artifact, so the scores are necessarily conservative.

This is a clean instance: users choose elements from three existing designs and combine them through a visible style-mixing panel. It makes selective multi-source fusion directly manipulable and is readily transferable to other generative-design domains, though style mixing itself was no longer wholly novel by 2024.
The quote characterizes semantic typographic logos as blending type and imagery, but provides no evidence of a UI in which users select existing operands and invoke a fusion operator.
ratings.disqualify_reason: The evidence describes the nature of the generated artifact, not the required pick-and-combine interaction.

ratings.reason: Although the quote explicitly mentions selected images and captions, the operation assembles heterogeneous assets into a post block rather than returning a fused result in the same space as its operands.
ratings.disqualify_reason: This is cross-modal post composition, not a same-space fusion of selected peer items under the pattern's structural signature.

ratings.reason: Fusing the contents gathered through a pen into a new image plausibly makes spatial, embodied recombination actionable. The quote identifies the user-controlled container and system response, but does not establish that its contents are two or more existing same-space operands or that operand selection is distinct from construction.

Interpolation is a canonical continuous pick-and-combine operation, and applying it to human-guided exploration of underrepresented data regions could materially affect augmentation. The evidence does not show how users select anchors, control the interpolation, or see the resulting samples, limiting mechanism and evidence scores.
The quote is a general definition of visual blends. It does not demonstrate an interface built by the authors, user selection of two objects, or an invoked fusion operation.
ratings.disqualify_reason: The supplied evidence is background characterization rather than evidence of the candidate system's interaction mechanism.

ratings.reason: Quologue produces a textual remix from a past highlight and a keyword response, an interesting use of synthesis for reflection. Yet the quote does not show users choosing two existing peer artifacts or invoking a reusable same-space combination operator; one operand appears newly elicited rather than picked.

Integrating family contributions into one composite image is a potentially consequential and non-obvious social use of fusion. The evidence does not specify the form of the contributions, how they are selected, or whether users explicitly invoke the operation, so it only weakly establishes the structural signature.

This is an unusually complete exemplar: users separately select two visible groups and invoke a named Mix operator to produce mixed styles. Group-to-group latent mixing on a spatial mood board is concrete, transferable, and more distinctive than a generic pairwise blend control.

Users bring target and reference images into a workspace, manipulate the references, and receive a generated image, giving the pattern visible operands and a controllable same-medium result. The quote does not explicitly name the fusion operator, and reference-conditioned image generation is a comparatively settled design move.

The combiner is a textbook discrete recombination operator: it takes two shoe images and creates a shoe using the upper from one and sole from the other. It is exceptionally legible but domain-bound and largely a straightforward component-swap implementation of an established idea.

The visible panel accepts one to three selected audio references and exposes adjustable weights for continuous fusion, closely matching every part of the signature. It offers meaningful fine-grained control and transfers readily across media, although weighted reference mixing is a mature interaction idea by 2025.

The paper content and a song blueprint are heterogeneous backend inputs used to generate lyrics, not selected peer items fused into a result in their own space. No visible choice or combination interaction is described.
ratings.disqualify_reason: The evidence describes a generation pipeline rather than the pattern's user-invoked, same-space fusion operator.

ratings.reason: Two parent sounds undergo a precisely specified crossover, with whole parameter groups swapped to create reusable child sounds. This is a clear discrete same-space recombination and an interesting way to make complex synthesizer settings explorable, though the quote does not explicitly show the user's selection and invocation steps.

A palette where prompt objects can be mixed and later detached makes fusion a reversible, material-like operation rather than a hidden prompt rewrite. That metaphor significantly moved generative-interface design and transfers beyond images, although the short quote omits the exact selection sequence and resulting mixed representation.

The upper-and-sole combiner is a very clean discrete fusion of two selected shoe designs into another shoe design. The fuller feasibility framing suggests more practical consequence than the earlier version, but the pattern move itself remains a familiar component-recombination technique and is somewhat product-specific.

Users do select multiple feedback units, but those units serve as instructions for generating a draft. The result is not in the same space as the selected operands and is not a fusion in which the operands are peer artifacts.
ratings.disqualify_reason: This is selected-constraint application to text generation, not same-space pick-and-combine.

ratings.reason: The quote reports that the system merges stylistic traits into sketches, but does not show designers visibly choosing source items or invoking an operator. Traits and output sketches are also described at different representational levels.
ratings.disqualify_reason: The evidence supports backend style fusion but not the required visible, user-invoked pick-and-combine interaction.

ratings.reason: Interpolation between explicit anchors with a decoding path back to input-space examples is a strong continuous instance and especially generalizable for model exploration. The mechanism is clear at an architectural level, but anchor selection and the mixing control are not described; by 2026, anchor interpolation itself is also well established.

Users first create and retain dance sequences, then select sequences from a gallery and blend them, directly satisfying separate selection, invocation, and same-space result requirements. Applying reusable fusion to temporal bodily sequences is more distinctive than another image-style mixer, though transfer requires domains with composable sequences.

Users identify features in multiple referenced products and explicitly compose them into a new product concept, making source selection and discrete recombination central. It materially broadens consumer design agency, though feature-to-image or feature-to-3D generation is not as strictly same-space as the pattern's strongest exemplars.
